correctness.rationale: For all integers p,q≥2, a full-measure extrema stratification and its explicitly computed \(r^{p-2}\) Jacobian give exactly a Beta(p−1,q+1) independent-product representation. Exact second moments on the S_p×S_q zero-sum and contrast sectors yield the three rational eigenvalues, including all normalizations. Euclidean anchored-to-zero-sum Jacobian \(1/\sqrt N\), determinant multiplication, uniform Stirling and beta–gamma/CLT prove volume, isotropic constant and independent fixed-p Gamma–Gaussian limits. The standalone source path verify_bipartite_covariance.py was run: eight independently rebuilt polytope configurations agree on exact rational total volumes and every covariance entry. Finite checks are corroboration only; the full theorem follows from the analytic proof. No unproved equalities enter the claim.

originality.rationale: Primary sources on exactly the same complete-bipartite graph give facet/Ehrhart volume and Banach–Mazur vertex-optimal quadratic results, which do not calculate interior moments. Nearby book-graph work covers only \(p=2\), and discrete integer height laws differ from continuous uniform volume; a similarly named two-level signed-chain body has extra coordinate restrictions and one extra dimension. Actual searches for covariance, exact beta disintegration, geometric isotropy, aliases and Gamma–Gaussian limits identified no implication of the whole statement. The conclusion is a qualified best-knowledge originality judgment, not a formal uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: An unindexed exact moment table, unpublished calculation or differently parametrized polar-body identity may already imply some or all formulas.
Search ranking does not prove exhaustiveness, especially for less common terms for uniform random Lipschitz functions.
The body is dual to the symmetric edge polytope; inadvertent comparison to results for the primal polytope is an additional bibliographic classification risk.

value.rationale: The theorem evaluates a canonical bulk second-order convex-body invariant in all dimensions for a natural two-parameter family of finite-dimensional Banach dual balls. The three invariant covariance sectors are exact and nontrivial, the beta representation gives an efficient exact sampler and integrated quadratic observables, and the uniform isotropic constant together with a fixed-side independent Gamma–Gaussian limit demonstrates structurally different scaling regimes. These results go beyond known face counts, volume recitations and simple low-dimensional instances, without claiming a paper-sized general theorem.
